The problem asks for the largest constant $C$ such that for all $\gamma > C$, Sun Wukong can guarantee victory in a turn-based game of flood containment on a grid.

Based on the analysis of the flood's perimeter growth, we found that for a diamond-shaped flood, the perimeter $P_n$ increases by 8 in each turn. In general, the perimeter growth rate of a flood is at most 8. Let $S_n$ be the set of flooded cells after turn $n$. The perimeter $P_n$ of $S_n$ satisfies $P_n \leq P_0 + 8n$, where $P_0$ is the initial perimeter.

Sun Wukong has a budget of $\gamma n$ walls after $n$ turns. He wins if he can eventually form a closed loop that encloses all flooded cells. The perimeter of the smallest such loop is at least the perimeter of the convex hull of the flooded cells. For any initial set of cells $S_0$, the flooded cells $S_n$ will be contained within a bounding box of size roughly $(L + 2n) \times (L + 2n)$, where $L$ is the initial diameter of $S_0$. The perimeter of this bounding box is $8n + 4L$.

To guarantee victory for any $S_0$ (and thus any $L$), Sun Wukong needs his budget $\gamma n$ to eventually exceed the perimeter $8n + 4L$. This is possible for all $L$ if and only if $\gamma > 8$. If $\gamma \leq 8$, the Sea God can choose an initial set $S_0$ with a large enough diameter $L$ such that $8n + 4L > \gamma n$ for all $n$.

Therefore, the largest constant $C$ is 8.
